t:
Section 521(b)(2)(E) is amended—
    (1) by inserting after “$10,000.” the following: “In the case of a motor carrier, the Secretary may also place the violator’s motor carrier operations out of service.”; and 
    (2) by striking “such penalty” after “It shall be a defense to” and inserting “a penalty”.

fable.w: This amendment expands the Secretary's enforcement power against violators and adjusts the wording of a defense to a penalty. The tempting reading is that "It shall be a defense to" gives an outside party a way to contest a federal decision, but that is a defense in an individual enforcement action, not consultation, comment, a hearing, or a granted right to sue over a federal policy decision. No outside party is consulted or brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: In the case of a motor carrier, the Secretary may also place the violator’s motor carrier operations out of service.

opus.w: This amendment adds an enforcement power: the Secretary may place a violating motor carrier out of service. It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or advisory body involving people outside the federal government. The wording change to 'It shall be a defense to a penalty' describes a defense in an enforcement action, not a granted right to sue over a federal policy decision, so the tempting litigation reading fails.
opus.s: In the case of a motor carrier, the Secretary may also place the violator’s motor carrier operations out of service.

It does not give anyone a right to sue over a policy decision. The new out-of-service power is a decision the Secretary makes alone, with no consultation, hearing, comment period or rulemaking.
